title: Okta Domain 5 questions (5.1, 5.2)
note: Original questions written for Delzar Certification Academy. Not from exam dumps or commercial banks; not affiliated with Okta.

questions.stem: A new hire's account was imported from the HR system and shows the status Staged. She has received no email from Okta and cannot sign in. What should the admin do FIRST?
choices: Reset the user's password and choose a temporary password
Unsuspend the user from the More Actions menu
Clear the user's sessions and revoke tokens
Activate the user so Okta can send the activation email
questions.answer: Activate the user so Okta can send the activation email
questions.explanation: A Staged user exists in Okta but has not been activated, so no activation email has been sent. Unsuspending only applies to a Suspended user, and a password reset does not activate the account.

questions.stem: A user's profile shows Pending user action. He says he deleted the welcome email before setting up his account. What is the BEST way to let him finish setup?
choices: Unlock the user account from the profile
Deactivate the user and then delete the account entirely
Resend the activation email from the user's profile
Reset the user's authenticators
questions.answer: Resend the activation email from the user's profile
questions.explanation: Pending user action means activation was sent but the user has not completed it, so resending the activation email is the fix. Unlocking applies only to a Locked out user.

questions.stem: An admin suspends a user who is on a leave of absence. Which statement describes the user's account while it stays Suspended?
choices: The user is removed from every app and must be provisioned again when unsuspended
The user cannot sign in, and app assignments and group memberships are kept
The user can sign in but sees an empty end-user dashboard
The user is unlocked automatically after the lockout period ends
questions.answer: The user cannot sign in, and app assignments and group memberships are kept
questions.explanation: Suspension blocks sign-in while keeping the account's assignments and memberships, so Unsuspend restores access as it was. Removing app access is what deactivation does, not suspension.

questions.stem: A user is shown as Locked out after several wrong password attempts. Which Okta Identity Engine policy sets how many failed attempts cause this status?
choices: The password policy that applies to the user's group
The default rule of the global session policy
The authenticator enrollment policy for the user
The authentication policy assigned to the Okta Dashboard app
questions.answer: The password policy that applies to the user's group
questions.explanation: Lockout thresholds are part of the password policy settings. The global session policy controls Okta sessions and the first factor, not the number of failed password attempts.

questions.stem: A user's status is Password expired because her password reached the maximum age set in policy. What happens the next time she signs in?
choices: She is blocked until an admin unlocks the account
She must set a new password after entering her current one
She must enroll Okta Verify again before she can sign in at all
She reaches the dashboard but every app tile is disabled
questions.answer: She must set a new password after entering her current one
questions.explanation: An expired password forces a password change during the next sign-in; no admin action is required. Admin unlock applies to a Locked out user, not an expired password.

questions.stem: A contractor's account shows Deactivated, and the manager asks the help desk to restore it because the contract was renewed. Which action allows the contractor to sign in again?
choices: Activate the user again and then check the app assignments
Unsuspend the user from the More Actions menu on the profile
Unlock the user from the user's profile
Clear the user's sessions and revoke tokens
questions.answer: Activate the user again and then check the app assignments
questions.explanation: A deactivated user must be activated again; Unsuspend and Unlock apply only to the Suspended and Locked out statuses. Deactivation removes app access, so the admin should confirm assignments afterward.

questions.stem: Which user status means an account was created by an admin, an import or the API but has not been activated yet?
choices: Pending user action
Suspended
Staged
Password reset
questions.answer: Staged
questions.explanation: Staged accounts exist but have not been activated. Pending user action comes later, after activation is sent and before the user finishes setting up the account.

questions.stem: On Monday morning every user sourced from Active Directory fails to sign in with a correct password, while Okta-sourced users sign in normally. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The global session policy has a new rule that denies all AD-sourced users
The password policy lockout threshold was set too low
Okta FastPass was turned off for the whole organization
No Okta AD agent is available to handle delegated authentication
questions.answer: No Okta AD agent is available to handle delegated authentication
questions.explanation: AD-sourced users with delegated authentication have their passwords checked by Active Directory through the Okta AD agents, so agents that are down affect only those users. A low lockout threshold would affect Okta-sourced users as well.

questions.stem: A sales manager is Locked out right before a customer meeting and calls the help desk. What should the help desk admin do to restore access immediately?
choices: Reset the user's Okta Verify authenticator
Suspend the user and then unsuspend the user
Select Unlock on the user's profile
Clear the user's sessions and revoke tokens
questions.answer: Select Unlock on the user's profile
questions.explanation: Unlock returns a Locked out user to Active straight away. Resetting authenticators or clearing sessions does not change the lockout status.

questions.stem: The service desk is flooded with lockout calls and wants users to recover from lockouts on their own. Which change BEST meets this goal?
choices: Raise the maximum lifetime in the global session policy
Add a deny rule to the Okta Dashboard authentication policy
Create a dynamic network zone for the office
Allow self-service unlock in the password policy rule
questions.answer: Allow self-service unlock in the password policy rule
questions.explanation: Self-service unlock is a password policy rule option that uses the allowed recovery authenticators. Session lifetime has no effect on whether a locked account can recover.

questions.stem: An admin must read a one-time password to a user over the phone and force the user to choose a new password when signing in. Which action should the admin take?
choices: Reset Password and send the password reset link by email
Reset Password and choose the temporary password option
Suspend the user and email the new password from Okta
Clear the user's sessions and choose to forget devices
questions.answer: Reset Password and choose the temporary password option
questions.explanation: The temporary password option shows a password the admin can pass on securely and marks the password as expired, so the user must change it at the next sign-in. A reset link is emailed, not read out.

questions.stem: An admin sends a password reset link to a user who is sourced from Active Directory. An hour later the user is still signing in with the old password. Why does this work?
choices: AD-sourced users keep using the existing password until they use the link
Okta keeps a cached copy of AD passwords for one day
The reset link failed because AD-sourced users can never be reset from Okta
The global session policy overrides any pending password reset
questions.answer: AD-sourced users keep using the existing password until they use the link
questions.explanation: For AD-sourced users, sending a reset link does not invalidate the current password until the user follows the link. Reset links do work for AD-sourced users when delegated authentication allows it.

questions.stem: A user reports that her password was phished. While resetting her password, the admin also wants every existing Okta session for her to end on all devices. What should the admin do?
choices: Choose to sign the user out of all sessions during the reset
Unlock the user before sending the reset link
Reset all of the user's authenticators instead of the password
Remove the user from every assigned app
questions.answer: Choose to sign the user out of all sessions during the reset
questions.explanation: The password reset dialog can also revoke all of the user's Okta sessions, which signs the user out on every device. Resetting authenticators does not change a stolen password.

questions.stem: Users who forget their password are only offered email for recovery, but the company also wants text message recovery. Phone is already active under Security > Authenticators. What should the admin change?
choices: Require Phone in the global session policy rule
Allow Phone as a recovery authenticator in the password policy
Add Phone to the authentication policy of each app the users open
Enable text messages in the Okta Verify settings
questions.answer: Allow Phone as a recovery authenticator in the password policy
questions.explanation: Recovery authenticators are chosen in the password policy rule. App authentication policies control access to apps, not the forgot-password flow.

questions.stem: Which standard administrator role is designed for staff who unlock accounts and reset passwords without broader configuration rights?
choices: Report Administrator
Application Administrator
Read-only Administrator
Help Desk Administrator
questions.answer: Help Desk Administrator
questions.explanation: Help Desk Administrators can reset passwords, unlock users and reset authenticators for the users in scope. Read-only and Report Administrators cannot change users at all.

questions.stem: An employee's laptop was stolen from a car while she was signed in to Okta. Her password is still safe, and the admin needs to end her Okta sessions right away. Which action should the admin take?
choices: Reset Password and send her a reset link
Deactivate her account and then delete it
Use Clear User Sessions on her profile
Use Reset Authenticators on her profile
questions.answer: Use Clear User Sessions on her profile
questions.explanation: Clear User Sessions ends her Okta sessions and revokes tokens without changing the password. Deactivating the account would also remove her app access for no reason.

questions.stem: After an admin clears a user's sessions, the user can still work in a SaaS app for a while before being asked to sign in again. What is the MOST likely explanation?
choices: Session clearing only takes effect after the next directory import
Keep me signed in overrides any admin request to clear sessions
Clearing sessions only affects sessions on mobile devices
The app keeps its own session, which lasts until it expires
questions.answer: The app keeps its own session, which lasts until it expires
questions.explanation: Clearing Okta sessions stops new SSO from Okta, but an app's own session lasts until it expires unless the app supports a logout integration such as Universal Logout. Directory imports are unrelated to sessions.

questions.stem: Security requires users to sign in to Okta again after 2 hours without activity. Where should the admin configure this?
choices: The re-authentication frequency in an app's authentication policy
The maximum password age in the password policy
The idle time setting in a global session policy rule
The settings of the authenticator enrollment policy
questions.answer: The idle time setting in a global session policy rule
questions.explanation: The global session policy rule controls the Okta session, including idle time and maximum lifetime. An app's re-authentication frequency only governs access to that app.

questions.stem: The finance app must ask for authentication every time it is opened, even when the user already has an Okta session. Which change BEST meets this without affecting other apps?
choices: Set the finance app's rule to prompt at every sign-in attempt
Shorten the global session policy lifetime for all users in the org
Clear every user's sessions on a nightly schedule
Lower the maximum password age in the password policy
questions.answer: Set the finance app's rule to prompt at every sign-in attempt
questions.explanation: Re-authentication frequency in the app's authentication policy rule applies to that app only. Shortening the global session lifetime would affect every app.

questions.stem: Users complain that closing the browser always forces them to sign in to Okta again. The company is fine with sessions that survive a browser restart. Which setting should the admin change?
choices: Turn on self-service unlock in the password policy rule for the users
Let global session cookies persist across browser sessions in the rule
Raise the re-authentication frequency for each app
Add the users to the Everyone group for the session
questions.answer: Let global session cookies persist across browser sessions in the rule
questions.explanation: A global session policy rule can make the Okta session cookie persist across browser sessions. App re-authentication settings do not keep the Okta session alive after the browser closes.

questions.stem: What does the Clear Sessions & Revoke Tokens action on a user's profile do?
choices: Resets the user's password and sends a reset link
Ends the user's Okta sessions and revokes the user's tokens
Removes the user from every group and app assignment the user has
Resets every authenticator the user has enrolled
questions.answer: Ends the user's Okta sessions and revokes the user's tokens
questions.explanation: The action signs the user out of Okta sessions and revokes the user's tokens without touching the password, groups or authenticators. A password reset is a separate action.

questions.stem: A user works without breaks all day and is still asked to sign in to Okta again exactly 12 hours after the first sign-in. What is the MOST likely reason?
choices: The idle timeout in the global session policy was reached at that time
The user's password expired at the 12-hour mark
An admin reset the user's Okta Verify authenticator
The maximum session lifetime in the global session policy was reached
questions.answer: The maximum session lifetime in the global session policy was reached
questions.explanation: Maximum session lifetime ends a session after a fixed time even while the user is active. The idle timeout only applies after a period without activity.

questions.stem: A user replaced his phone and wiped the old one. He can no longer approve Okta Verify prompts and cannot sign in. What should the help desk admin do?
choices: Clear the user's sessions and revoke tokens
Unlock the user account from the profile
Reset the user's Okta Verify enrollment
Deactivate the user and then activate the user
questions.answer: Reset the user's Okta Verify enrollment
questions.explanation: Resetting the Okta Verify enrollment lets the user enroll the new phone at the next sign-in. Clearing sessions does nothing about a lost authenticator.

questions.stem: Members of the Sales group are never asked to set up Okta Verify. Their authenticator enrollment policy lists Okta Verify as Disabled. What should the admin change?
choices: Set Okta Verify to Optional or Required in the policy for Sales
Add Okta Verify to the global session policy rule for the Sales group
Add the Sales group to the password policy
Create a network zone for the Sales offices
questions.answer: Set Okta Verify to Optional or Required in the policy for Sales
questions.explanation: The authenticator enrollment policy decides which authenticators a group can or must enroll. Global session and password policies do not control enrollment.

questions.stem: An admin wants users to enroll Google Authenticator, but it does not appear as a choice in the authenticator enrollment policy. What is the MOST likely reason?
choices: The global session policy blocks third-party authenticators
It has not been added under Security > Authenticators yet
Only Super Administrators can see that enrollment policy
Google Authenticator needs a dynamic network zone first
questions.answer: It has not been added under Security > Authenticators yet
questions.explanation: An authenticator must be added and active in Security > Authenticators before enrollment policies can list it. Policy visibility does not depend on the admin role in this way.

questions.stem: An app's authentication policy rule requires a phishing-resistant authenticator. A user has enrolled only a password and SMS, and the enrollment policy that applies to him allows nothing stronger. What happens when he opens the app?
choices: He is denied because no allowed authenticator meets the rule
Okta lets him in with SMS and writes a warning event to the log
Okta lowers the requirement to password and SMS
Okta enrolls a security key for him automatically
questions.answer: He is denied because no allowed authenticator meets the rule
questions.explanation: Okta never downgrades an authentication policy requirement; if the user cannot enroll an authenticator that meets the rule, access is denied. SMS is not phishing resistant.

questions.stem: Where in the Admin Console does an admin reset a single user's enrolled authenticators?
choices: In Security > Authenticators, by deactivating that authenticator type
In Directory > Profile Editor, on the user profile
On the user's profile, under More Actions > Reset Authenticators
In Reports, from the MFA Usage report
questions.answer: On the user's profile, under More Actions > Reset Authenticators
questions.explanation: Resetting authenticators is done per user from the user's profile. Deactivating an authenticator in Security > Authenticators would affect every user in the org.

questions.stem: A user belongs to both Contractors and Employees. Two authenticator enrollment policies exist, and the Contractors policy is listed first. The user keeps getting the Contractors requirements. Why?
choices: Okta merges both policies and applies the strictest of the settings
Okta always applies the most recently edited policy
The default policy overrides every custom policy
The Contractors policy has higher priority and matches first
questions.answer: The Contractors policy has higher priority and matches first
questions.explanation: Policies are evaluated in priority order and the first one that matches the user applies. Okta does not merge enrollment policies.

questions.stem: A user lost her FIDO2 security key but still uses Okta Verify every day. The admin wants her to enroll a replacement key without disturbing Okta Verify. What should the admin do?
choices: Reset every authenticator the user has enrolled
Deactivate the FIDO2 authenticator for every user in the whole org
Reset only the security key authenticator for that user
Clear the user's sessions and revoke tokens
questions.answer: Reset only the security key authenticator for that user
questions.explanation: Reset Authenticators lets the admin choose which enrollment to remove, so only the lost key is reset. Deactivating the authenticator org-wide would affect everyone.

questions.stem: A user traveling abroad is blocked before she can even enter her password, while colleagues in the office sign in normally. The org has a network zone on its blocklist. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: Her current IP address falls inside a blocklisted network zone
Her password expired while she was traveling abroad
Her Okta Verify enrollment was reset by the help desk during the trip
Her app assignments were removed by a group rule
questions.answer: Her current IP address falls inside a blocklisted network zone
questions.explanation: Requests from blocklisted zones are rejected before authentication starts, which matches being blocked before the password prompt. An expired password would be shown after the password step.

questions.stem: A global session policy has a rule at priority 1 that denies sign-in from outside the country, and a rule at priority 2 that allows the Executives group from anywhere. A traveling executive is denied. What should the admin do?
choices: Add the executive to the Everyone group
Raise the session lifetime in the deny rule
Delete the default rule of the policy
Move the Executives rule above the rule that denies sign-in
questions.answer: Move the Executives rule above the rule that denies sign-in
questions.explanation: Rules are checked from the top, and the first rule that matches is used, so the deny rule wins today. Placing the exception first lets it match before the deny rule.

questions.stem: Users enrolled in Okta FastPass for passwordless sign-in are still asked for a password before anything else. What is the MOST likely configuration cause?
choices: The password policy has a short maximum password age
The global session policy rule requires a password to start the session
Okta Verify is set to Optional instead of Required in the enrollment policy
The app authentication policy allows any two factors
questions.answer: The global session policy rule requires a password to start the session
questions.explanation: The global session policy rule decides whether a password is required to establish the Okta session; it must allow any factor from the app's rules for passwordless sign-in. Password age does not change the first prompt.

questions.stem: Before going live, an admin wants to see which app sign-in policy rule a specific user would match from a given IP address and platform. Which tool should the admin use?
choices: The System Log CSV export
The Okta Password Health report
The Profile Editor preview
The Access Testing Tool
questions.answer: The Access Testing Tool
questions.explanation: The Access Testing Tool simulates a request and shows which policies and rules would match. The System Log only shows what already happened.

questions.stem: A user belongs to groups that are assigned to two different global session policies. Which policy applies when the user signs in?
choices: The policy that was created most recently
Both policies, combined so the strictest rule from each one applies
The highest-priority policy whose assignment includes the user
The default policy, whenever several policies match
questions.answer: The highest-priority policy whose assignment includes the user
questions.explanation: Okta evaluates policies in priority order and applies the first one assigned to a group the user belongs to. Policies are not combined.

questions.stem: Users who connect through a commercial VPN service were suddenly blocked after an admin changed network settings. The admin had just created a dynamic zone that matches anonymizing proxies. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The VPN's exit addresses match the dynamic zone used in a deny rule
The VPN changes users' passwords when they connect
Dynamic zones reset the Okta Verify enrollment of each user who connects
The VPN removes users from the group assigned to the app
questions.answer: The VPN's exit addresses match the dynamic zone used in a deny rule
questions.explanation: Dynamic zones can match anonymizing proxies such as many commercial VPNs, so a deny rule using that zone blocks those users. VPNs do not change Okta credentials or group membership.

questions.stem: A user calls because she cannot sign in. Put the troubleshooting steps in the order an admin should follow.
items: Open the user's profile and check her status
Search the System Log for her recent failed events
Read the outcome reason and the policy that was involved
Apply the fix, such as unlocking or resetting the password
Ask her to sign in again and confirm a successful event
questions.explanation: Status is the fastest clue, the System Log then shows the actual failure and its reason, and only after that should the admin change anything. Confirming a successful event closes the ticket with evidence.

questions.stem: An attacker phished a user's password and may already be signed in as that user. Which TWO actions end the attacker's existing access and stop the stolen password from being used again?
choices: Clear the user's sessions and revoke tokens
Reset the user's password
Resend the user's activation email
Unlock the user's account
Raise the global session lifetime
answers: Clear the user's sessions and revoke tokens
questions.explanation: Clearing sessions ends what the attacker already has, and a password reset makes the stolen password useless. Activation emails and unlocking do neither.

questions.stem: Match each user status to the description that BEST fits it.

pairs.match: Activation sent but setup not finished
Sign-in blocked by an admin with assignments kept
Must choose a new password at the next sign-in

targets_extra: Waiting for a manager to approve the account
questions.explanation: Each status points to a different fix: activate, resend activation, unlock, unsuspend or let the user change the password. Okta has no status for manager approval of an account.

questions.stem: A user says the expense app is missing from her dashboard, while her teammates see it. What should the admin check FIRST?
choices: Whether status.okta.com shows an active incident for the org's cell
Whether the app's SAML certificate expired
Whether she is assigned to the app individually or through a group
Whether her password is close to expiring
questions.answer: Whether she is assigned to the app individually or through a group
questions.explanation: A tile appears only for users assigned to the app, directly or through a group, so assignment is the first check when one person is affected. A certificate or Okta incident would affect everyone.

questions.stem: After an admin edited an app's settings, every assigned user lost the app's tile, although the admin can still see the users on the Assignments tab. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The setting that hides the application icon from users was turned on
The app's group assignments were converted to individual assignments
The global session lifetime was reduced for all users
Self-service unlock was turned off in the password policy
questions.answer: The setting that hides the application icon from users was turned on
questions.explanation: Apps have a visibility option that hides the icon from users even though they remain assigned. Converting assignments would not remove anyone's tile.

questions.stem: During maintenance an admin deactivated an app integration. Users still assigned to it now report that the tile has disappeared. What should the admin do when the maintenance ends?
choices: Reassign every user to the app individually
Clear all of the users' Okta sessions
Recreate the group that is assigned to the app
Activate the app integration again
questions.answer: Activate the app integration again
questions.explanation: An inactive app is hidden from users, so activating it again restores access. The assignments are still in place, so reassigning users is unnecessary work.

questions.stem: Where can an admin see every app assigned to one user and whether each assignment is individual or comes from a group?
choices: The Profile Editor entry for the user's Okta profile
The Applications tab of the user's profile
The group rules page in Directory
The Okta Usage report under Reports
questions.answer: The Applications tab of the user's profile
questions.explanation: The user's Applications tab lists each assigned app with how it was assigned. The Okta Usage report shows sign-ins, not assignments.

questions.stem: An admin removes the Marketing group from an app's assignments, but one marketing employee still sees the app. What is the MOST likely reason?
choices: Group removals take effect only after the next password change
The employee also has an individual assignment to the app
The employee's Okta session keeps the tile until it expires
Removing a group never affects users who are already signed in
questions.answer: The employee also has an individual assignment to the app
questions.explanation: Individual and group assignments are independent, so the user keeps the app through the individual assignment. Group removals do not wait for a password change.

questions.stem: An app has hundreds of individual assignments, and the admin wants them to be managed through a group instead. Which feature on the app's Assignments tab helps with this?
choices: Prioritize groups
Push groups
Convert assignments
Import users
questions.answer: Convert assignments
questions.explanation: Convert assignments changes individual assignments into group-based ones for users who are in the assigned group. Group priority only decides which group's attribute values win.

questions.stem: An admin created a group rule that should place all Austin employees in the Austin Office group, but nobody has been added. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The rule was saved but never activated
Group rules only add users who are created after the rule
The Austin Office group must be assigned to an app first
Group rules run only once a week on a fixed schedule
questions.answer: The rule was saved but never activated
questions.explanation: A new group rule is inactive until the admin activates it, and only then does it evaluate users. Active rules also evaluate existing users, not just new ones.

questions.stem: A group rule adds users whose department is exactly Engineering. A user whose department is set to Engineering Team was not added. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: Group rules never evaluate the department attribute
The user must sign in once before any group rule can evaluate him
The user's password policy blocks group membership
The user's department value does not match the rule's expression
questions.answer: The user's department value does not match the rule's expression
questions.explanation: The rule compares the attribute value with its condition, and Engineering Team does not equal Engineering. Department is a standard attribute that rules can use.

questions.stem: An admin tries to remove a user from a group, but the option is unavailable because a group rule added the user. What should the admin do?
choices: Delete the group and create a new group with the same name and apps
Suspend the user so the rule releases the membership
Reset the user's password so the rule evaluates again
Change the user's attribute or exclude the user in the group rule
questions.answer: Change the user's attribute or exclude the user in the group rule
questions.explanation: Memberships managed by a rule cannot be removed by hand; the user must stop matching the rule or be listed as an exception. Deleting the group would affect every member.

questions.stem: An admin needs to change the condition of a group rule that is currently active. What must the admin do FIRST?
choices: Deactivate the rule so it can be edited
Remove every user the rule has added
Delete the target group of the rule
Clear the sessions of the affected users
questions.answer: Deactivate the rule so it can be edited
questions.explanation: Okta requires an active rule to be deactivated before it can be edited, and then activated again. Removing users by hand is neither needed nor possible for rule-managed members.

questions.stem: A user moved from Finance to Sales. A rule added her to the Sales group, but she still has access to Finance apps. Her Finance membership was added manually years ago. Why does she still have Finance access?
choices: Group rules keep old memberships for 30 days by default
Users can belong to only one group at any time
The manual Finance membership is not removed by attribute changes
The Sales rule copies her old memberships into the new Sales group
questions.answer: The manual Finance membership is not removed by attribute changes
questions.explanation: Group rules manage only the memberships they create, so a manual membership stays until an admin removes it. Users can belong to many groups.

questions.stem: A group rule adds everyone in the Sales department to Sales Tools, but the company's chief executive, who is listed in Sales, must not be included. What is the BEST way to handle this?
choices: Remove the executive from the group by hand each week
List the executive as an exception in the group rule
Change the executive's status to Suspended
Create a second rule that removes the executive
questions.answer: List the executive as an exception in the group rule
questions.explanation: Group rules can exclude named users, which keeps them out even when they match the condition. Manual removal is not possible for rule-managed memberships, and rules only add users.

questions.stem: A team's apps are assigned to a group that a group rule fills based on the title attribute. HR has not yet set the title on a new hire's profile. Why does the new hire have none of the team's apps?
choices: Group rules only evaluate users once a month
Apps assigned to rule-based groups require approval
The rule must be recreated whenever a new user is added to Okta
He does not match the rule until his title is filled in
questions.answer: He does not match the rule until his title is filled in
questions.explanation: A rule adds a user only when the user's attributes match its condition, so an empty title means no membership and no apps. Rules evaluate again when the profile is updated.

questions.stem: An admin cannot add a user to the HR-Staff group in Okta, and the group's source is shown as Active Directory. How should the membership be changed?
choices: Make a copy of the group in Okta and add the user to the copy
Assign the user to the group with the Group Membership Administrator role
Add the user to the group in AD and let the next import update Okta
Use a group rule to place the user into the AD-sourced group
questions.answer: Add the user to the group in AD and let the next import update Okta
questions.explanation: Membership of AD-sourced groups is mastered in Active Directory and arrives in Okta through imports. Group rules cannot target directory-sourced groups.

questions.stem: When building a group rule, an admin cannot choose an AD-sourced group as the target in the Assign to field. Why?
choices: Group rules can only assign users to Okta-sourced groups
The admin needs the Report Administrator role to choose that group
AD-sourced groups first need an authentication policy
Group rules can only target groups assigned to an app
questions.answer: Group rules can only assign users to Okta-sourced groups
questions.explanation: Rules write membership only into groups that Okta masters. A directory or app controls membership of the groups it sources.

questions.stem: An admin sees a group with an app's logo next to its name and cannot edit its members in Okta. What kind of group is this?
choices: An Okta group that a group rule has locked
An app group whose membership comes from that app
The built-in Everyone group in the org
A group that was hidden by the app's visibility setting
questions.answer: An app group whose membership comes from that app
questions.explanation: Groups imported from an app are mastered by that app, so their membership is read-only in Okta. Rule-managed memberships are a property of individual users, not of a whole group's type.

questions.stem: Which type of group lets an admin manage membership directly in Okta, both by hand and with group rules?
choices: Okta-sourced groups
Groups sourced from Active Directory
Groups imported from an LDAP directory
Groups imported from a connected app
questions.answer: Okta-sourced groups
questions.explanation: Okta groups are mastered in Okta, so admins can add members manually or with rules. Directory and app groups take membership from their source.

questions.stem: A user was added to an AD security group this morning, but in Okta she still is not a member of the matching AD-sourced group. What is the MOST likely reason?
choices: Okta removes AD group members who have not signed in
No import from Active Directory has run since the change
AD-sourced groups only change when a group rule runs
The user must reset her password before she can join any new group
questions.answer: No import from Active Directory has run since the change
questions.explanation: Changes to AD-sourced groups appear in Okta after the next import. Group rules cannot change AD-sourced groups.

questions.stem: A contractor can see an internal payroll app because an admin assigned the app to the Everyone group by mistake. What should the admin do?
choices: Remove the contractor from the Everyone group
Hide the app's icon from every user in the org
Assign the app to a narrower Okta group and remove Everyone
Deactivate the contractor's account in Okta
questions.answer: Assign the app to a narrower Okta group and remove Everyone
questions.explanation: Everyone is a built-in group that contains all users and cannot be edited, so the fix is a more specific assignment. Hiding the icon leaves access in place.

questions.stem: A user was assigned to an app with provisioning, but no account was created in the app. On the Provisioning tab, the To App setting for Create Users is turned off. What should the admin do?
choices: Add the user to the Everyone group in Okta
Clear the user's sessions and revoke tokens
Reset the user's password with a temporary password and retry it
Turn on Create Users in the app's To App provisioning settings
questions.answer: Turn on Create Users in the app's To App provisioning settings
questions.explanation: Without Create Users, Okta assigns the app but does not create the account in it. Group membership in Everyone does not trigger provisioning.

questions.stem: Several assignments to a provisioning-enabled app failed overnight. Where can an admin review the failed provisioning tasks and retry them?
choices: In the Profile Editor for that app
In the Tasks list on the Admin Console dashboard
In the authenticator enrollment policy for the app
On the Okta status page for the org
questions.answer: In the Tasks list on the Admin Console dashboard
questions.explanation: Failed provisioning tasks appear in the Admin Console Tasks list, where they can be retried or closed. The Profile Editor holds attributes, not task results.

questions.stem: Provisioning to an app started failing for every user right after the app's owner rotated its API token. What should the admin do?
choices: Turn off Create Users and turn it back on again
Remove every user from the app and then assign them all again
Change the app's sign-in method from SAML to SWA
Enter the new token in the provisioning settings and test it
questions.answer: Enter the new token in the provisioning settings and test it
questions.explanation: Provisioning uses the stored API credentials, which are now invalid; updating and testing them restores the connection. Toggling features does not fix credentials.

questions.stem: Two groups are assigned to the same app with different role values, and a user who belongs to both receives the role from the wrong group. What controls which value the user gets?
choices: The date when each group was first created
The user's status shown on the profile
The group priority order on the app's Assignments tab
The order in which the user enrolled authenticators in Okta
questions.answer: The group priority order on the app's Assignments tab
questions.explanation: When a user is in several groups assigned to one app, group priority decides whose attribute values are used. Group creation date plays no part.

questions.stem: A user's last name changed in Okta, but the app with provisioning still shows the old name a week later. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: Update User Attributes is not enabled for the app
Create Users is not enabled for the app
The user's password has not been reset yet
The app is hidden from the user's dashboard
questions.answer: Update User Attributes is not enabled for the app
questions.explanation: Update User Attributes pushes profile changes to existing app accounts. Create Users only matters when the app account is first created.

questions.stem: Besides the Super Administrator, which standard administrator role can close or retry failed provisioning tasks?
choices: Help Desk Administrator
Application Administrator
Group Administrator
Read-only Administrator
questions.answer: Application Administrator
questions.explanation: Okta's role comparison lists closing and retrying tasks for Super Administrators and Application Administrators. Help Desk and Read-only Administrators cannot manage app tasks.

questions.stem: A departed employee was deactivated in Okta, but her account in a provisioning-enabled app is still active. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: Her Okta sessions were not cleared before the deactivation took place
The app was hidden from her dashboard before she left
She was never part of the Everyone group in Okta
Deactivate Users is not enabled in the app's provisioning settings
questions.answer: Deactivate Users is not enabled in the app's provisioning settings
questions.explanation: Okta deactivates the app account only when the Deactivate Users feature is on. Clearing sessions does not affect the account in the app.

questions.topic: App Sign-In Failures and Policy Denials
questions.stem: A user is assigned to a SAML app and sees its tile, but when he opens it the app shows a user-not-found error. Other users sign in fine. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The app username Okta sends for him is not one the app knows
The app's SAML signing certificate expired for every user of the app
His Okta password expired while the app was open
The Okta status page lists an incident for the org
questions.answer: The app username Okta sends for him is not one the app knows
questions.explanation: The value Okta sends as the user's identifier comes from the app username, and a mismatch makes the app reject only that user. An expired certificate would break sign-in for everyone.

questions.topic: App Sign-In Failures and Policy Denials
questions.stem: Right after Okta's SAML signing certificate for an app was rotated, every user fails at the app with a signature error. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The users' Okta passwords all expired at the same time as the rotation
Group rules removed the users from the app
The app still trusts the previous Okta signing certificate
The app's icon was hidden from the users
questions.answer: The app still trusts the previous Okta signing certificate
questions.explanation: The app must be updated with the new certificate or metadata, or it rejects every signed assertion. Group or password changes would not produce a signature error.

questions.topic: App Sign-In Failures and Policy Denials
questions.stem: When a user tries to open an OIDC app, Okta reports that the user is not assigned to the client application. What should the admin do?
choices: Reset the user's authenticators from the profile
Unlock the user account from the profile
Raise the global session lifetime for the user
Assign the user, or a group the user is in, to the app
questions.answer: Assign the user, or a group the user is in, to the app
questions.explanation: The message means the user has no assignment to the app integration. Authenticators and session lifetime have nothing to do with assignment.

questions.topic: App Sign-In Failures and Policy Denials
questions.stem: A user can open the HR app from the office but is denied when working from home. She is assigned to the app and her status is Active. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: Her app assignment is removed every evening by a scheduled group rule run
The app's authentication policy denies access outside the office zone
Her password expires whenever she leaves the office
The app's icon is hidden for users outside the office
questions.answer: The app's authentication policy denies access outside the office zone
questions.explanation: App authentication policy rules can use network zones, so off-network requests can be denied while assignment stays in place. Group rules do not change by location.

questions.topic: App Sign-In Failures and Policy Denials
questions.stem: A SWA app opens from the tile, but the app always rejects the user's sign-in because the stored credentials are outdated. The app is set so that users enter their own username and password. What is the BEST fix?
choices: Switch the app's sign-in method from SWA to SAML for that user
Clear the user's Okta sessions and revoke tokens
Have the user update the app credentials stored in Okta
Reset the user's Okta password with a reset link
questions.answer: Have the user update the app credentials stored in Okta
questions.explanation: With SWA, Okta replays the credentials it holds, so the user should update them when the app password changes. The Okta password is a different credential.

questions.topic: App Sign-In Failures and Policy Denials
questions.stem: Signing in from the Okta dashboard to a SAML app works, but starting from the app's own login page fails before users reach Okta. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The Okta sign-in URL configured in the app for SP-initiated SSO is wrong
The users are not assigned to the app in Okta
The app's icon is hidden from the dashboard
The global session policy denies sign-in requests that start at the app's page
questions.answer: The Okta sign-in URL configured in the app for SP-initiated SSO is wrong
questions.explanation: IdP-initiated sign-in works, which proves assignment and the assertion are fine; SP-initiated sign-in depends on the app sending users to the correct Okta URL. Unassigned users would fail both ways.

questions.topic: App Sign-In Failures and Policy Denials
questions.stem: A user signs in to Okta with a password and is later asked for Okta Verify only when opening the payroll app. What explains the extra prompt?
choices: The payroll app's authentication policy requires an extra authenticator
The global session expired at the exact moment the payroll app was opened
The user's password expired when the app opened
A group rule removed the user from the payroll app
questions.answer: The payroll app's authentication policy requires an extra authenticator
questions.explanation: Each app's authentication policy can demand more assurance than the Okta session already has, which triggers a step-up prompt. A removed assignment would deny access rather than ask for Okta Verify.

questions.stem: A user cannot find an app on her dashboard. Put the checks in the order that moves from the user outward.
items: Confirm that the user's status is Active
Check whether she is assigned to the app individually or through a group
If the assignment is through a group, confirm her membership and any group rule
Check that the app is active and its icon is not hidden
Review the System Log for her attempts to open the app
questions.explanation: An inactive user sees nothing, so status comes first; then the assignment, how it is granted, the app's own state, and finally the events for anything still unexplained.

questions.stem: A group rule should add everyone in the Marketing department to the Marketing Apps group, but a new marketing hire was not added. Which TWO causes are MOST likely?
choices: The rule is still inactive
The hire's department value does not match the rule's condition
The hire is a member of the Everyone group
The Marketing app's icon is hidden
The hire's password has expired
answers: The hire's department value does not match the rule's condition
questions.explanation: An inactive rule adds nobody, and a rule only adds users whose attributes match its condition. Everyone membership, icon visibility and password status do not affect group rules.

questions.stem: Match each symptom to its MOST likely cause.

pairs.item: The tile is missing for one user only
pairs.match: The user is not assigned to the app

pairs.item: The tile is missing for every assigned user
pairs.match: The app's icon is hidden from users

pairs.item: The user is assigned but has no account in the app
The user receives the role from the wrong group
The admin cannot remove the user from a group
pairs.match: The membership is managed by a group rule

targets_extra: The global session lifetime is too long
questions.explanation: Assignment, visibility, provisioning features, group priority and rule-managed membership each produce a distinct symptom. Session lifetime does not hide apps or change memberships.
